attempts.narrative: Three turns, four to zero, no player damage beyond Life Orb recoil and one Air Slash. Jolteon's Thunderbolt removed Finneon before its Tailwind resolved, then Wattrel, then Mantyke at 4x; Kartana's Leaf Blade closed on Arrokuda. Every member of this team is Water or Water/Flying except the bird, so a single Electric special attacker covers the whole roster.

strategy_checks.check: Finneon's Tailwind can charge Wattrel before Thunderbolt; execution order, not a flag, decides the same-turn benefit
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 1 Finneon selected Tailwind - the correct opening for the authored plan - but a 2x Thunderbolt knocked it out before the move resolved. Correctly, no Wind Power charge was granted to Wattrel from a Tailwind that never happened.

strategy_checks.check: Wind Power must be gained and consumed natively
strategy_checks.evidence: No wind move ever landed, and Wattrel never behaved as though charged. Its Air Slash on turn 2 did ordinary damage.

strategy_checks.check: Soak conversion is used only when it has a payoff, and never merely to weaken Arrokuda's Water damage
strategy_checks.evidence: Finneon died on turn 1 and Soak was never selected. My leads were Electric and Grass/Steel, neither of which has a Ground typing worth removing, so declining Soak would have been correct in any case.

strategy_checks.check: Mantyke supplies Wide Guard and the alternate Surf/Storm Drain lane; Surf must be reconsidered beside every partner
strategy_checks.evidence: Mantyke entered on turn 2 and was knocked out by a 4x Thunderbolt on turn 3 before acting. Notably it did NOT select Surf beside a Water-typed Arrokuda partner that does not absorb Water, which is the error the dossier warns against - it chose Air Slash.

strategy_checks.check: Arrokuda uses Propeller Tail to ignore eligible redirection while applying physical pressure
strategy_checks.evidence: Arrokuda chose Protect on both of its turns and never attacked. See AI observations.

strategy_checks.check: Storm Drain and Water Absorb hold the Water lane
strategy_checks.evidence: I deliberately brought no Water attack, so neither absorber had anything to absorb. Both abilities were present and correctly did nothing.

protect_ledger.payoff: real - Finneon died to Thunderbolt first, so Kartana's Leaf Blade redirected onto Wattrel and the guard blocked it
real - blocked a 2x Leaf Blade on the turn it entered
EMPTY - the second consecutive Protect failed and Arrokuda was knocked out by the same Leaf Blade it had guarded against the previous turn, having never attacked

ai_observations: Arrokuda spent both of its turns on Protect, the second consecutively at full HP, and contributed nothing to the battle. Under the no-read expected-value model the first guard is defensible; repeating it into the known reduced success rate, while holding a Mystic Water Liquidation and Propeller Tail specifically authored to punch through redirection, is the weakest sequence I saw. Worth a look at the PAIR_GUARD constants for a full-HP attacker whose partner is also unthreatened.
Mantyke correctly declined Surf beside a non-absorbing Water partner, which is the exact ally-damage trap the dossier flags.

level_changes.rule_applied: Won on the first attempt in three turns with zero faints. Brief rule: +1 on the weakest one or two members.
level_changes.verification: Offset-only edits; move legality and strategy coherence are unaffected. --write deliberately not run because a concurrent session has unrelated authored edits in the same tree.

level_changes.note: Two levels will not change this result. The problem is type coverage, not numbers - see the cooler note.

cooler_note: The coastal wind-and-current concept is genuinely distinctive and a clear improvement on the rain quartet it replaced; Soak plus Wind Power plus Propeller Tail is three real mechanics in a four-member route team, which is more than most route trainers attempt. The fatal flaw is that all four members are Water or Water/Flying, so one Electric attacker is 2x or 4x into the entire roster and the fight is over in three turns before any of those three mechanics can fire. A concrete suggestion for a later pass (not applied here): swap one member for a non-Water body that still fits the sea-breeze theme and punishes the obvious Electric answer - a Ground or Grass coastal species would make the player pay for bringing a single Electric sweeper, and would give Finneon's Soak a target whose typing is actually worth converting. Keep Finneon, Wattrel and the Soak plan; the roster needs a body that is not on the Electric menu.

evidence.scope: Synthetic headless benchmark through scripts/playthrough/battle_driver.py against work/agent-battle-build. Not earned campaign play.
